Mobile phones have now become universal devices with which we can do almost anything and perform nearly any task, thanks to the emergence of mobile applications. Mobile software development attracts the attention of different companies, and many Xamarin developers or hybrid app development is becoming more and more popular and demanded. As of March 2017, there are over 2.8 million available mobile apps on the Google Play Store and over 2.2 million available apps on the Apple Play Store, forming a huge catalog of applications users can choose from. In fact, in today’s world, websites are no longer enough for businesses to stay on top and reach the largest possible audience; having a mobile app has now also become a standard that enables customers and businesses to connect and interact quickly and on the fly.

With mobile applications becoming an essential component for many businesses, the need for tools that can make mobile app development a faster and more cost-effective process has become increasingly critical. In this article, we take a look at PhoneGap, a tool that does just this.

Things You Should Know Before You Hire PhoneGap App Developer

PhoneGap allows the creation of hybrid mobile applications just from HTML, CSS, and JavaScript codes. It was first developed in 2009 by Nitobi at an iPhoneDevCamp event, and since then, it has become a prominent name among mobile developers. In 2011, Adobe acquired Nitobi and released PhoneGap’s open-source core as Apache Cordova, but kept PhoneGap as a product built on top of Cordova, offering additional features on top of those available from the open-source distribution. According to AppBrain, PhoneGap currently holds a market share of 6.70% among all mobile applications. Its largest market share lies in the business category of applications, in which it holds a 17.41% market share. Moreover, according to BuiltWith, PhoneGap’s user base comes mostly from the United States, Canada, Germany, Spain, and Australia.

Hybrid App Platform Comparison

With so many other options for hybrid mobile app development, confusion may arise as to the differences among these frameworks. You might be wondering: what are the differences between PhoneGap vs Cordova, PhoneGap vs Ionic, or PhoneGap vs Xamarin? To put it simply, all of these are platforms for developing hybrid mobile applications. Cordova provides the core technology that powers both PhoneGap and Ionic, as well as many other frameworks. Let’s look at a brief comparison of some specific features of these four frameworks.

PhoneGap App Samples You Should Check Before Your Hire PhoneGap Programmer

Here are some interesting applications built by PhoneGap developers using the PhoneGap framework:

FanReact is a mobile app for sports fans who love to interact and share experiences with other fans all over the world. It allows its users to engage in group discussions about their favorite teams, share their thoughts on the different games and moves by their favorite players, and even upload their reaction photos or videos during gameplay.

Localeur is a recommendation and rating app for restaurants and bars that focuses on authenticity by only allowing locals to rate the food establishments in their own cities. In this way, it allows its travelers and tourists to get credible recommendations straight from the local residents of each city they visit.

Snowbuddy is a social mobile app for the snowsport enthusiast. It records the user’s various skiing statistics like top speed, distance traveled, duration played, and calories burned and allow them to share these with each other. It even allows users to post skiing challenges to one another.

BrowserQuest is a multiplayer mobile adventure game. In it, you control a young warrior across different lands with dangerous monsters and precious treasures. This game can be played alone or with friends, allowing players from all over the world to battle each other in the quest for supremacy.

My Heart Camera is a fancy camera and photo editing app whose theme focuses on hearts. It allows users to apply different filters and add heart stickers and decors to their photos, and then share or post them onto various social platforms like Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, LINE, and Tumblr.

Tools PhoneGap Specialist Is Using

PhoneGap developers are the key to the successful and quick development of a mobile application for your business. A great PhoneGap developer must be highly capable of using the different PhoneGap tools at their disposal, such as:

  • PhoneGap CLI – The PhoneGap Command Line Interface (CLI) gives developers full control and flexibility over their applications. Written in Node.js, the PhoneGap CLI lets users utilize the command line terminal to perform various tasks such as compiling, running, or creating files on the server.
  • PhoneGap Desktop – An alternative to the CLI is the PhoneGap Desktop application, which bakes in a graphical user interface (GUI) to facilitate the implementation of the various PhoneGap functionalities. The desktop app has access to the same PhoneGap plugins and libraries as the CLI version of the PhoneGap app.
  • PhoneGap Mobile Developer – This app enables developers to run their current app in a mobile environment to see how it behaves and looks. Changes done on the code are automatically reflected in the mobile environment so developers won’t have to re-compile after every modification.
  • PhoneGap Build – This is a cloud-hosted platform that enables developers to simply upload HTML, JavaScript, and CSS files of working web applications and have them automatically converted and packaged into working mobile applications. The platform also maintains native SDKs automatically, so they get updated every time an update is released.

PhoneGap Programmer Salary: How Much It Costs to Hire PhoneGap App Developers

The power of hybrid mobile development lies in its ability to dramatically reduce the cost of mobile app development. In order to maximize this reduction in cost, it’s also important to hire PhoneGap developers that offer the best rates. For this purpose, let’s make a comparison of the salaries of PhoneGap developers in different countries to see where it’s best to hire from. We use PayScale as our data source. Since salary information specific to PhoneGap developers is not available, we instead use salary information on mobile app development teams in general. In particular, we compare the salaries of developers with 1-4 years of experience. While the actual values may not be highly accurate, we expect the relative values in different countries to be correct.

According to PayScale, the average gross annual salaries of mobile app developers are as follows:

  • US – $72,052
  • Netherlands – €33,511 ($39,521)
  • UK – £29,779 ($39,977)
  • Ukraine – $18,000
  • Australia – AU$57,916 ($44,386)


Comparison of Average Gross Annual Salaries of Mobile App Developers in Different Countries (Source: PayScale)

From the above values, it is highly evident that Ukraine offers by far the best rates for mobile application development teams.
